g.text: Moccasin: retention intervals in a constraint program

g.title: main contribution moccasin constraint programming formulation tensor rematerialization
g.desc: The paper's main contribution is Moccasin, a constraint programming formulation of tensor rematerialization.
g.text: Moccasin — a constraint programming (CP) formulation of tensor rematerialization.

g.title: central idea represent each node decisions small number retention intervals start end event tensor lifetime reduces discrete variables quadratic linear number nodes
g.desc: Its central idea is to represent each node's decisions as a small number of retention intervals, defined by the start and end event of the tensor's lifetime, which reduces the count of discrete variables from quadratic to linear in the number of nodes.
g.text: Represent each node's decisions as a few
retention intervals — a start and end event

g.title: authors show how encode nonlinear memory precedence constraints standard cp building blocks cumulative reservoir constraints optional variant enforces input topological ordering reduce search space
g.desc: On top of this, the authors show how to encode the nonlinear memory and precedence constraints using standard CP building blocks, the cumulative and reservoir constraints, and they add an optional variant that enforces an input topological ordering to further reduce the search space.
g.text: encoded with two off-the-shelf CP primitives:
Optional: enforce an input topological ordering
to further shrink the search space.

g.title: payoff up to order-of-magnitude speedup over prior work large graphs
g.desc: The payoff is up to an order-of-magnitude speedup over prior work on large graphs.
g.text: Up to an order-of-magnitude speedup over
prior work on large compute graphs.
